note: An example lane plan. `laneRole` is closed: a `family` lane is bounded by an ownership row derived from the canonical inventory, a `domain` lane by a synthetic row over a region no family owns, and an `integrator` — the only role that may declare its own writeRoot — by a declared shared region. F2/F3 are the interesting case: `structure/workspace/search-command-bar` lives INSIDE `structure/workspace/connected-command-palette`'s source owner, and the two lanes are disjoint only because the outer row's writeExcludes is derived from that nesting. Nothing declares it; move either family in the inventory and the bound moves with it. B is the shared-CSS holder for this plan, and it is the only one: a shared domain admits one claimant even when the files differ.
